pairs.source_text: Sic vocibus consulis, terrore praesentis exercitus, minis amicorum Pompei plerique compulsi inviti et coacti Scipionis sententiam sequuntur: uti ante certam diem Caesar exercitum dimittat; si non faciat, eum adversus rem publicam facturum videri. Intercedit M. Antonius, Q. Cassius, tribuni plebis.
pairs.question: Qui duo tribuni plebis sententiae, ut Caesar exercitum dimitteret, intercesserunt?
pairs.question_en: Which two tribunes of the plebs vetoed the motion that Caesar should disband his army?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to the senate's decree that Caesar disband his army; the two named tribunes (Mark Antony and Q. Cassius Longinus) who interposed the veto are given verbatim ('Intercedit M. Antonius, Q. Cassius, tribuni plebis'). The veto and the tribunes' subsequent flight to Caesar are the iconic opening of the civil war; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Profugiunt statim ex urbe tribuni plebis seseque ad Caesarem conferunt. Is eo tempore erat Ravennae exspectabatque suis lenissimis postulatis responsa.
pairs.question: In quo oppido erat Caesar, cum tribuni plebis ex urbe profugientes ad eum se contulerunt?
pairs.question_en: In what town was Caesar when the tribunes of the plebs fled the city and came to him?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to Caesar and the fleeing tribunes; locative answer supported verbatim by 'Is eo tempore erat Ravennae'. Caesar's position at Ravenna at the outbreak of the war is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Conclamant legionis XIII, quae aderat, milites—hanc enim initio tumultus evocaverat, reliquae nondum convenerant—sese paratos esse imperatoris sui tribunorumque plebis iniurias defendere.
pairs.question: Cuius legionis milites, quae sola initio tumultus aderat, se paratos esse Caesaris tribunorumque plebis iniurias defendere conclamaverunt?
pairs.question_en: The soldiers of which legion, the only one present at the start of the disturbance, shouted that they were ready to defend the wrongs done to Caesar and the tribunes of the plebs?
pairs.derivation: Number/name fact anchored to Caesar and the start of the war; answer (legio XIII) supported verbatim, including 'quae aderat' and 'reliquae nondum convenerant' (only the Thirteenth was present). The legion that crossed the Rubicon with Caesar; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Cognita militum voluntate Ariminum cum ea legione proficiscitur ibique tribunos plebis, qui ad eum profugerant, convenit.
pairs.question: In quod oppidum Caesar cum legione XIII primum profectus est, ubi tribunos plebis profugos convenit?
pairs.question_en: To which town did Caesar first advance with the Thirteenth Legion, where he met the fugitive tribunes of the plebs?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to Caesar and the Thirteenth Legion; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Ariminum cum ea legione proficiscitur ibique tribunos plebis ... convenit'. Caesar's first seizure across the Rubicon; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Cum his ad Domitium Ahenobarbum Corfinium magnis itineribus pervenit Caesaremque adesse cum legionibus duabus nuntiat.
pairs.question: Ad quem Pompeianorum ducem Caesar Corfinium magnis itineribus pervenit?
pairs.question_en: Against which Pompeian commander did Caesar march to Corfinium by forced marches?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Corfinium and Caesar; single named answer supported verbatim by 'ad Domitium Ahenobarbum Corfinium ... pervenit' (the praenomen L. given at 1.23). Domitius Ahenobarbus, besieged at Corfinium and there pardoned by Caesar, is closed-book history.

pairs.source_text: Pompeius his rebus cognitis, quae erant ad Corfinium gestae, Luceria proficiscitur Canusium atque inde Brundisium.
pairs.question: In quod oppidum maritimum Pompeius, cognitis rebus ad Corfinium gestis, Luceria per Canusium se recepit?
pairs.question_en: To which coastal town did Pompey withdraw, by way of Luceria and Canusium, once he learned of the events at Corfinium?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to Pompey and Corfinium; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Luceria proficiscitur Canusium atque inde Brundisium'. Pompey's retreat to Brundisium is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Reperit consules Dyrrachium profectos cum magna parte exercitus, Pompeium remanere Brundisii cum cohortibus viginti.
pairs.question: Quo profectos esse consules Caesar, Brundisium cum legionibus perveniens, repperit?
pairs.question_en: Where had the consuls departed to, as Caesar found when he arrived at Brundisium with his legions?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to the consuls, Brundisium, and Caesar; single answer supported verbatim by 'consules Dyrrachium profectos'. The consuls' crossing of the Adriatic to Greece is closed-book. Acc.+inf. 'profectos esse' under repperit.

pairs.source_text: Mittit in Sardiniam cum legione una Valerium legatum, in Siciliam Curionem pro praetore cum legionibus duabus; eundem, cum Siciliam recepisset, protinus in Africam traducere exercitum iubet. Sardiniam obtinebat M. Cotta, Siciliam M. Cato; Africam sorte Tubero obtinere debebat.
pairs.question: Quis ex Pompeianis Siciliam obtinebat, quam Caesar Curionem occupare iussit?
pairs.question_en: Who held Sicily for the Pompeians, the province Caesar ordered Curio to seize?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Sicily and Curio; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Siciliam M. Cato [obtinebat]', with Curio sent there with two legions. Cato Uticensis abandoning Sicily before Curio is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Quibus effectis armatisque diebus XXX, a qua die materia caesa est, adductisque Massiliam his D. Brutum praeficit, C. Trebonium legatum ad oppugnationem Massiliae relinquit.
pairs.question: Quem legatum Caesar ad oppugnationem Massiliae reliquit?
pairs.question_en: Which legate did Caesar leave in charge of the siege of Massilia?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Massilia and Caesar; single named answer supported verbatim by 'C. Trebonium legatum ad oppugnationem Massiliae relinquit' (D. Brutus being set over the fleet). The siege of Massilia under Trebonius is closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Afranius et Petreius et Varro, legati Pompei, quorum unus Hispaniam citeriorem tribus legionibus, alter ulteriorem a saltu Castulonensi ad Anam duabus legionibus, tertius ab Ana Vettonum agrum Lusitaniamque pari numero legionum optinebat.
pairs.question: Qui tres legati Pompei initio belli civilis Hispanias obtinebant?
pairs.question_en: Which three legates of Pompey held the Spanish provinces at the outbreak of the civil war?
pairs.derivation: Name fact anchored to Pompey and the Spanish provinces; the three named legates are given verbatim ('Afranius et Petreius et Varro, legati Pompei'). Pompey's Spanish command is closed-book; answer is the closed set of three.

pairs.source_text: Quibus coactis celeriter Petreius per Vettones ad Afranium pervenit, constituuntque communi consilio bellum ad Ilerdam propter ipsius opportunitatem gerere.
pairs.question: Ad quod oppidum Afranius et Petreius communi consilio bellum gerere constituerunt?
pairs.question_en: At which town did Afranius and Petreius jointly decide to wage the war?
pairs.derivation: Place fact anchored to Afranius and Petreius; single named answer supported verbatim by 'bellum ad Ilerdam ... gerere'. The campaign of Ilerda is the central episode of Book I; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Caesar legiones in Hispaniam praemiserat VI, auxilia peditum V milia, equitum III milia.
pairs.question: Quot legiones Caesar in Hispaniam praemisit?
pairs.question_en: How many legions did Caesar send ahead into Spain?
pairs.derivation: Number fact anchored to Caesar and Spain; answer (VI = six) supported verbatim by 'legiones in Hispaniam praemiserat VI' and echoed at 1.85 ('sex legiones ... missas in Hispaniam'). Closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Fabius finitimarum civitatum animos litteris nuntiisque temptabat. In Sicori flumine pontes effecerat duos distantes inter se milia passuum IIII.
pairs.question: In quo flumine apud Ilerdam C. Fabius, Caesaris legatus, duos pontes effecit?
pairs.question_en: In which river near Ilerda did Caesar's legate Gaius Fabius build two bridges?
pairs.derivation: Geography fact anchored to Fabius and Ilerda; single named answer supported verbatim by 'In Sicori flumine pontes effecerat duos'. The Sicoris (Segre) is the river of the Ilerda campaign; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Petreius atque Afranius cum stipendium ab legionibus paene seditione facta flagitarentur, cuius illi diem nondum venisse dicerent, Caesar ut cognosceret, postulatum est, eoque utrique, quod statuit, contenti fuerunt. Parte circiter tertia exercitus eo biduo dimissa duas legiones suas antecedere, reliquas subsequi iussit, ut non longo inter se spatio castra facerent, eique negotio Q. Fufium Calenum legatum praeficit. Hoc eius praescripto ex Hispania ad Varum flumen est iter factum, atque ibi reliqua pars exercitus dimissa est.
pairs.question: Ad quod flumen exercitus Afranii et Petreii in Hispania victus a Caesare dimissus est?
pairs.question_en: To which river was the defeated army of Afranius and Petreius led from Spain and disbanded?
pairs.derivation: Place/outcome fact anchored to Afranius and Petreius (named in the same paragraph) and Spain; single named answer supported verbatim by 'ex Hispania ad Varum flumen est iter factum, atque ibi reliqua pars exercitus dimissa est'. The surrender and disbandment of the Pompeian army in Spain is the climax of Book I; closed-book.
